claim_tested: Which Arabidopsis proteins need MIA40 in planta
key_finding: mia40 insertional mutants lack CSD1 and CCS, have reduced complex I, lack peroxisomal CSD3 and reduced AIM1; AtMIA40 is in mitochondria and peroxisomes; no visible mutant phenotype
context: A. thaliana, whole plant, T-DNA insertion lines
confidence_limitations: High for the phenotype; the affected proteins are not shown to be direct substrates

direction: refutes the premise that motif class drives dependence
claim_tested: Can plant ERV1 oxidise IMS proteins without Mia40
key_finding: Plant Erv1 promotes IMS protein import and oxidative folding independently of Mia40; it cannot oxidise yeast Mia40 and blocks it
context: Recombinant AtERV1, yeast erv1/mia40 mutants, in vitro reconstitution
confidence_limitations: High for the biochemistry; heterologous yeast context

claim_tested: Is a canonical twin-CX9C substrate MIA40-independent in plants
key_finding: Glutathione at physiological concentration and redox potential supports AtERV1 oxidation of COX19 and CCMH without MIA40
context: Recombinant At and yeast MIA40/ERV1, cysteine alkylation and cytochrome c reduction
confidence_limitations: High; in vitro only, no in planta flux measurement

claim_tested: What determines MIA40 dependence of a non-twin-motif substrate
key_finding: Yeast Ccs1 lacks twin CxnC motifs yet depends on Mia40/Erv1; a single structural disulfide C27-C64 is the docking determinant
context: S. cerevisiae, mitochondrial import assays, cysteine mutants
confidence_limitations: High in yeast; determinant shown here not to be conserved in plant or human CCS

claim_tested: Which Ccs1 cysteines interact with Mia40
key_finding: Ccs1 C27 and C64 in domain I are critical for mitochondrial import and Mia40 interaction; dispensable for cytosolic Ccs1 activity

claim_tested: Is the CCS/SOD1 node a conserved disulfide-relay substrate
key_finding: Mia40 depletion lowers Ccs1 and Sod1; Mia40 overexpression raises them; Mia40 forms mixed disulfides with Ccs1
confidence_limitations: High; shows the dependent class is conserved and motif-free

claim_tested: Is SOD1 dependence downstream of CCS
key_finding: CCS mitochondrial distribution is regulated by Mia40/Erv1 and CCS promotes SOD1 maturation and retention in the IMS
confidence_limitations: Review-level; the primary data are in PMID 18703498

claim_tested: Does CCS localization control SOD1 import
key_finding: CCS localization determines SOD1 partitioning; the Mia40/Erv1 pathway participates in CCS mitochondrial import

claim_tested: Is SOD1 redox state set by the glutathione pool
key_finding: SOD1 redox state is controlled by CCS in a pathway not linked to the GSH redox potential
context: Human and bacterial cells, in-cell NMR

claim_tested: Does any other Arabidopsis protein require MIA40
key_finding: AtSLP2 is IMS-localized, interacts with AtMIA40, and its phosphatase activity requires AtMIA40 and disulfide formation
confidence_limitations: Medium-high; activity dependence, not import dependence

claim_tested: Do cysteine motifs separate the two sets
key_finding: twin CX3C/CX9C 0/5 dependent vs 7/9 independent (p=0.021) but in the reverse direction; collapses to p=0.350 when the five complex I twin-CX9C subunits are counted as dependent; upstream hydrophobic feature p=0.58-1.00; compartment separates equally well (p=0.031)
context: UniProt canonical sequences, UP000006548 (39,144 entries), Fisher exact
confidence_limitations: Direct computation; sets are tiny and collinear with compartment
